study.title: Effect of acupuncture treatment for patients with knee osteoarthritis on brain fluctuation amplitude and functional connectivity: a randomized three-armed fMRI study
study.randomization: Eligible patients were randomly assigned to acupuncture group (AG), sham-acupuncture group (SG), or waiting list group (WG) in a ratio of 1:1:1. The randomization sequence was generated using SAS software (version 9.3) by an independent researcher.
study.blinding: Acupuncturists were not blinded to the allocation for successfully performing acupuncture treatment. However, they were not allowed to discuss the intervention type with patients. The patients, MRI operators, outcome evaluators, and statisticians were all blinded to group assignment.
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) 45 to 65 years old; (2) knee pain lasts at least 6 months; (3) KL (Kellgren-Lawrence) grade II or III in recent 12 months; (4) numerical rating scale (NRS)≥4 in the past week; (5) right-handedness
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) history of knee replacement, waiting surgery, arthroscopy within 1 year or intra-articular injection within 6 months, and discomfort of knee joint caused by other reasons; (2) serious organic pathological changes, mental abnormalities, psychiatric or neurological disorders, or coagulation disorders; (3) MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia; (4) received acupuncture or massage treatment in recent 1 month; (5) allergy to needles and alcohol or fear to acupuncture, and participated in other clinical studies in the past 3 months
study.source_location: pages 2-3, Materials and methods, Participants section

extraction_notes.note: No quantitative de qi or sensory experience scale data (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) were reported. De qi was described qualitatively as required in AG and not required in SG. No instrument for measuring de qi/sensations was mentioned.

Expectancy, treatment credibility, and blinding success (participant guessing of allocation) were not assessed or reported in this study. This is a notable limitation for interpreting nonspecific/placebo effects.
Adverse events were not reported in this paper. No mention of adverse events section or statement that no adverse events occurred was found.
The paper reports that voxel size for rs-fMRI is '3.5×3.5×3.5 mm [3]' — the '[3]' appears to be a citation rather than part of the measurement. The voxel size should be read as 3.5×3.5×3.5 mm.

The paper states 'DPBAI software' in one place (ALFF analysis section) and 'DPABI, version 6.1' in the preprocessing section. These appear to refer to the same software (DPABI), with 'DPBAI' likely being a typographic error in the original PDF.
extraction_notes.source_location: page 4, MRI data preprocessing and Brain metrics analysis sections

extraction_notes.note: The paper does not explicitly state whether fMRI data were acquired before or after the treatment sessions (i.e., on the same day as treatment or on separate days). The study design figure (Fig. 1A) suggests scans were done at baseline and after completion of the 4-week treatment block.

The specific anatomical locations of the 7 non-acupoints (NA1-NA7) used in the sham acupuncture group are only shown in Fig. 1B and are not described in text. Their precise anatomical locations could not be extracted with certainty from the figure.

The paper reports both Spearman rho (main analysis) and Pearson r (partial correlation controlling for gender and duration) for ALFF-NRS correlations. These are reported as separate analyses. Both have been extracted.
extraction_notes.source_location: pages 6-7, Correlation between altered ALFF and clinical symptoms section

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports that participants in the WG received 12 sessions of acupuncture as free compensation after the 4-week observation period, but no neuroimaging or clinical outcome data from this post-observation acupuncture period were reported.

The 'n_analyzed' for between-group comparisons (e.g., AG vs. SG = 52, SG vs. WG = 47) has been inferred by summing the group-specific n values (27+25=52; 25+22=47). These were not explicitly stated as the analysis n for each pairwise comparison.
No PMID was provided in the paper. The DOI is given in the header.

The paper mentions 'FOV=224 mm × 224 mm' and 'in-plane resolution=64×64' for the rs-fMRI sequence, which are not extracted into a separate FOV field since the template only captures voxel_size_exact. These additional acquisition parameters are noted here for completeness.

The paper uses 'ES' (effect size) throughout and states effect sizes 'were depicted as Cohen's d', but for some comparisons the Mann-Whitney U test was used, which would typically yield a rank-biserial correlation or similar non-parametric effect size. The authors computed these at https://www.psychometrica.de/effect_size.html. The exact computation method is unclear.
extraction_notes.source_location: pages 5-6, Clinical data statistical analysis section; Tables 2 and 3
